'''Ruku Kooff''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] sales executive.

==Biography==
A female Rodian who belonged to a clan that was sentenced for extermination by [[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red]], she adopted the false identity of Ruku Kooff, and lived under this for years, unbeknownst to her companions. 

Ruku Kooff was a member of a sales team that included [[Teeko Soonca]] and [[Mannee Swaano]]. While she was particularly friendly to [[Human/Legends|humans]], Ruku could barely tolerate her coworker, Mannee. 

During a hunting outing with her coworkers and off-world business associates, Mannee, who suspected her real origin, informed some [[Chattza clan/Legends|Chattza]] [[Protector (Rin'na)|Protectors]] they met in a [[hunting lodge]].

After the group had to deal with strange instances of sabotage, they were stranded in the [[jungle/Legends|jungle]]. On their way back to the lodge, they had to pass through a [[cave/Legends|cavern]] where they were ambushed and Ruku was killed by a group of Rodian [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. The rest of the hunting party were forced to leave her body behind in order to beat a hasty retreat. It was later revealed to her companions by Navik's Protectors that Ruku was "a criminal" and thereby sentenced to death.

Ruku, however, had faked her death, planning a safe passage off [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]]. She stowed away in a weapons crate of their off-world associates, who were leaving Rodia after their business trip. She planned to begin a new life somewhere in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Personality and traits==
Ruku Kooff was a friendly Rodian female, hiding in plain sight with her false identity. Her given name had not yet been revealed. Ruku was fond of a [[Chak-root/Legends|chak-root]] snuff that had a scent similar to rotting refuse. She had a peculiar&mdash;yet not uncommon among Rodians&mdash;speech impediment in which she had difficulty with pronouncing the ''"hyu-"'' syllable, instead vocalizing it as ''"hoo-"'', for example saying ''"hoo-mans"'' rather than ''"humans."''
